description: Fetch a public web page and return only the part you need instead of the raw HTML. view: markdown (main content, navigation and boilerplate removed), outline (headings), links (all links; query keeps those whose URL or text contains it), tables (one table, chosen by table, as a markdown table), find (only passages mentioning query; query required). Use this for any single page; use read_package_info for PyPI, npm and crates.io, and run_pipeline for multi-step extraction (e.g. filtering a table's rows). Reads the live page each call and doesn't run JavaScript, so pages built in the browser may come back thin. Only public http(s) addresses. Fetches are limited to 60 a minute per client. Errors (unreachable site, non-HTML content, no table at that index) come back with a suggested fix. Each call runs a built-in page recipe and is recorded in its public run statistics; otherwise nothing is kept except the result's handle, for 60 minutes.

max_tokens.description: Most tokens to return. markdown is trimmed (and marks the cut); other views return a preview and handle instead.

query.description: find: the word or phrase to look for (required). links: keep links whose URL or text contains it.

url.description: Public http(s) URL of the page.

name: read_page

handle.description: Handle id (h_...) of the full result, for run_op or read_handle.

preview.description: Instead of value, when the result is over max_tokens.

value.description: markdown/outline: text. links: [{href, text}]. tables: markdown table. find: [{match, context, line, offset}].

warning.description: The result looks wrong for this view, e.g. empty.
